Here are a few pcap files I used:

For Maps, Sets, Verbatim String and Null: [resp3.pcapng](/uploads/0701f64f09c32157c9c78d8a289516ce/resp3.pcapng)

For Boolean (forged packets): [resp_bool.pcapng](/uploads/864d3a62170d6ea054e4a8bf16d8b157/resp_bool.pcapng)

For Double (forged packets): [resp_double.pcapng](/uploads/49dd299a0c5471970988beabce2fe438/resp_double.pcapng)

For Big Numbers (forged packets): [resp_big_number.pcapng](/uploads/2dc1e86aea2d1fe159bfd60667148dda/resp_big_number.pcapng)
Can you edit this post so that the first file shows up. It might need a space or something. The Map dissection is particularly tricky.
The Map dissection is tricky enough (and essentially independent from supporting the other types) that it might be faster to get this approved if this were split into multiple MRs.

You cannot use `proto_tree_add_string` on a `hf_resp_boolean`, which is a FT_BOOLEAN.
Passing in `CRLF_LENGTH` as the length instead of the full length in the packet is incorrect as well. Usually in this sort of situation it would be appropriate to add an expert info instead.

changed this line in [version 6 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22992/diffs?diff_id=1630235720&start_sha=6749fe8c450d368848778626fe085bc5ef07e8ae#36e8d18f640c33d83d0b75de14257eac4e06e2c7_137_137)
This could just be `proto_tree_add_boolean`.
Some compilers might need a default case with `DISSECTOR_ASSERT_NOT_REACHED();`.
Possibly should have an expert info if the string_length is nonzero, as I understand the protocol.
Ideally should have an expert info if this fails.

Thank you for the review @johnthacker!

I agree with all notes and will make the appropriate changes. I shall ping you again once that's done.
